deploy.description: Readwise Reader 'Document Tags Updated' -> when a document is tagged `sendtonotion`, create an 'Article Share' idea in the Notion Social Content data source. Deduped through a free Zapier Table (Reader document id -> Notion page id) so a document is only ever turned into a page once. Migrated from the classic multi-step Zap of the same name (paused since 2026-08-29).

trigger.trigger_note: Catch hook. The sender is a Readwise webhook (Readwise's webhook settings) subscribed to the Reader `tags_updated` event, which POSTs the document object (top-level `id`, `title`, `source_url`, `tags` keyed by slug, `event_type`, `secret`). `webhook_url` is what that Readwise webhook must POST to; `trigger_url` is Zapier-internal and answers an unauthenticated POST with 401.
trigger.why_not_app_trigger: Switched 2026-10-01 from the Readwise Reader app trigger (`App228555CLIAPI@1.0.3` / `document_tag_updated`, on the d.chiuten@icloud.com Reader connection). That trigger is a REST hook (Zapier subscribed `https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/standard/20495893/21f32aab2b074e47be8523778e320f46/` in Readwise), but the durable dedupe layer from Zapier bug W6ZE93-VMEWP keyed every delivery on the document id, so a document fired once ever. Reader's auto-tagging on save consumed that one firing, and a later `sendtonotion` tag was dropped: 5 of the 9 documents tagged between 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-29 were missed (backfilled 2026-10-01). A raw catch hook bypasses the app trigger's dedupe.
trigger.dedupe_probe: UNVERIFIED: whether the durable dedupe layer also keys catch-hook deliveries on a payload's top-level `id` (Readwise's payload carries the document id there). After the publish, POST the same non-`sendtonotion` payload twice to `webhook_url`; two `not-tagged` runs means the fix holds. One run means it does not, and the fallback is a scheduled Reader-vs-dedup-Table sweep.
